title: Balanced Binary Tree
prompt:
Return whether a binary tree is **height-balanced**: for every node, its two subtrees' heights differ by at most 1.

**Example**: `[3,9,20,null,null,15,7]` → `true`; `[1,2,2,3,3,null,null,4,4]` → `false`.

Compute heights bottom-up, using a sentinel `-1` to signal 'already unbalanced' so you don't recompute.
hints: Write a helper returning subtree height, or -1 if any subtree below is unbalanced.
If either child returns -1, propagate -1 up immediately (short-circuit).
If `abs(leftH - rightH) > 1`, this node is unbalanced → return -1. Balanced overall ⟺ helper(root) != -1.

solution.explanation: O(n). Overloading the height value with a -1 'poison' means one post-order pass both measures heights and detects imbalance — no separate O(n) height call per node (which would make the naive version O(n²)).
